svg.title: AI-Driven Ansible Automation on AWS — Reference Architecture
svg.desc: Event-driven AIOps reference architecture. Filebeat and Kafka detect an Apache failure; Event-Driven Ansible triggers an enrichment workflow that calls a Granite model for root cause analysis; a human approves the generated prompt; a second workflow generates, commits and applies the remediation playbook.
svg.text: Event-driven self-healing infrastructure on AWS · Ansible Automation Platform 2.6 · RHEL 10 · Granite on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Default-deny security groups · ingress scoped to the operator /32, never 0.0.0.0/0 · IMDSv2 enforced · EBS encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key
RHEL 10 · m6i.2xlarge · 8 vCPU / 32 GiB · Podman Quadlet
Configured as code — 10 job templates · 2 workflows · 6 credentials
PostgreSQL and Redis run alongside in the containerized topology

THE AIOPS LOOP — WHAT HAPPENS, IN ORDER
A job template inserts an invalid directive into httpd.conf and restarts the service.
The restart fails by design — this is the incident.
Filebeat ships the httpd error log to Kafka. No polling and no cron — the platform
The EDA rulebook matches the shutdown event and launches the enrichment
workflow. Unattended from here until step 5.
Collect journal logs, ask the chat model for a root cause analysis and a one-line
fix instruction, then post both to Mattermost.
The AI-authored prompt is pre-filled in a survey. A person reviews it and decides.
Nothing is generated until they do.
The code model turns the approved prompt into a playbook. It is sanitised, committed
to Gitea, then synced back into AAP.
A job template runs the generated playbook with an explicit limit. Deliberate and
bounded — the natural place for a change window.
Apache serves again. Detection, RCA, generated remediation, a Git audit trail and a
human decision — in roughly ten minutes.
